clue.text: I want you to have this, you'd better believe it!

definitions.text: I want you to have this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: said when handing over a gift
second meaning: said to vouch for what you are telling someone

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves read as one generous speech, but each is a separate sense of the same four-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works literally as an offer to hand something over and idiomatically as an assurance that the speaker's word can be trusted.

clue.text: Picture commercial vehicle drawn along

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short advertisement for a forthcoming film
second meaning: an unpowered wagon towed behind a car or lorry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial vehicle' looks like one phrase, a van or lorry; the split falls between 'commercial' and 'vehicle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema advert previewing a film and a towed wagon share the same name.

clue.text: Race and colour related

parts.note: a kind is a sort or race of beings, as in humankind
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A remark linking race and colour, as in a discussion of ethnicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred as an adjective describes people connected by family or similar nature.

clue.text: Where cod and haddock may be found, generally

definitions.text: Where cod and haddock may be found
definitions.meaning: first meaning: out in the open sea, the main being an old word for the ocean
second meaning: on the whole, for the most part

explanation.walkthrough: The main is a poetic word for the high sea, so fish are literally located there; the same phrase is an everyday adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mostly or as a rule, which is what generally means too.

clue.text: Plant life for all, almost entirely destroyed

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the phrase before it loses its final letter
something entirely destroyed is wrecked to pieces, so the remaining letters are scrambled

parts.note: the two words run together, minus their final letter

explanation.surface: A grim note that plant life, which belongs to everyone, has been nearly wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost entirely' looks like one phrase; in fact 'almost' trims the words before it and 'entirely destroyed' smashes up what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the collective term for the plants of a region or period.

clue.text: Oust top rogue, settlement far off

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means wayward or out of control, so the letters stray from their order

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A call to depose a crooked leader, set in some remote colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' reads as a noun, the top rogue to be ousted, but it acts as an adjective meaning wayward.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small remote station or settlement far from the centre.

clue.text: Fee for securing boat — what might make lower charge?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the charge for tying up a vessel at a berth
second meaning, read as two parts: a lower is a cow that lows, and its fury, a moo plus rage, might make it charge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like 'reduce', but it is a cow, the animal that lows; split the answer as MOO RAGE and a furious cow charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring a boat at a harbour incurs a fee, called by this word.

clue.text: Make a lot of noise, and work on loft extension?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cheer or shout very loudly
second meaning, taken literally: building upward to enlarge an attic

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal second reading of an idiom: extending a loft might mean lifting the top of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a crowd so loud that it seems to lift the building's top.

clue.text: In competition with range in street

parts.note: an Aga is a brand of cooking range, a heavy stove
taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: It reads like a description of rival traders, one with a cooker for sale in the high street.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a British-made cast-iron range cooker, a familiar crossword stand-in for 'range'.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing against someone means competing with them as an opponent.

clue.text: No longer fashionable style — that's a point of view

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion
a look is a style, as in a new look

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing a dated style as merely a matter of opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlook is a person's general attitude or way of seeing things.

clue.text: Understand — as should a conductor?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: be aware of the real situation
second meaning, taken literally: an orchestra conductor ought to be familiar with the written music

explanation.walkthrough: A score is the full written music an orchestra plays from, so the idiom is literally true of a conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be aware of the facts of a situation, which is to understand it.

clue.text: Spend a lot, investing fifty in poisonous plant

indicators.note: to invest originally means to clothe or envelop, so one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: spurge is a plant with toxic milky sap
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A warning against throwing money at a dubious botanical venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' looks financial, matching 'spend', but it means clothing or surrounding: the plant wraps round the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend money extravagantly on something.

clue.text: Send back cold eggs, a cook producing salad ingredient

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the words that follow are read from right to left

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
ova is the Latin plural for eggs
taken as written
to do food is to cook it, as in meat done well

explanation.surface: A diner returns cold eggs and the cook makes something else instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocado is a fruit commonly sliced into salads.

clue.text: Ready to drop it after revolution, communist

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the little word before it is flipped end to end

parts.note: taken as written
red is a familiar label for a communist

explanation.surface: A communist, exhausted after the revolution, ready to put something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop it' looks like an order, but 'Ready to drop' is the definition and 'it' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ready to drop is exhausted, about to collapse from fatigue.

clue.text: Flat month in a pattern that's unusual

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for the time period among the other letters before they are mixed
unusual means out of the normal order, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters as printed
M is the abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: A dull month spent in an odd routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an adjective about the month, but it is the noun for a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartment is the American and general word for a self-contained flat.

clue.text: Love a tandoori for cooking

indicators.note: cooking mixes and transforms ingredients, so the letters of the dish are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A confession of passion for Indian clay-oven cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' can be a verb in the surface; as the definition it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and devotion.

clue.text: Ten operas composed in largely unknown language

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are assembled into a fresh order

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A composer writing ten operas in an obscure tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international language that few people actually speak.

clue.text: Bridge game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a floating bridge supported on boats
second meaning: a card game, also called twenty-one or blackjack

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge game' looks like the card game bridge, but it splits into two meanings; pontoon is the British name for blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a temporary floating crossing and a card game aiming for twenty-one.

clue.text: Awful hurry to rescue leaders in British banking industry

indicators.note: a rescuer gathers someone up and holds them safe, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: to rush is to hurry

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A bitter remark about a frantic bailout of the people at the top of British banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' as an adjective means awful in British slang, which keeps the part of speech fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something rubbish in everyday British speech means it is very poor or worthless.

clue.text: Endless beauty approaching English locale

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the following word is dropped

parts.note: Venus is the goddess of beauty, cut short of her last letter
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An endlessly beautiful English spot coming into view.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is a place where an event happens, a locale.

clue.text: Person turning up mask has it covered

indicators.note: having something covered means enclosing it, so the short word sits inside the face covering

parts.note: a visor is a mask or face shield on a helmet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone arrives in a mask that has everything under control.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone who calls round or arrives somewhere.

clue.text: Figure twelve required to catch horse

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so the animal is held inside the time of day

parts.note: noon is twelve o'clock midday
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A dozen people needed to round up a runaway horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' is the geometric shape, not a number, though 'twelve' pulls that way.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a plane figure with nine sides.

clue.text: Book passenger vehicle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a volume collecting several works
second meaning: the full old name for a bus

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' reads as a verb, reserving a seat on transport; it is the noun for a collected volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an anthology volume and the horse-drawn ancestor of the bus.

clue.text: Hold up seat in church

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to delay or stop progress
second meaning: a fixed seat for clergy or choir in a chancel

explanation.walkthrough: A choir stall is the enclosed seat for clergy and choristers in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to delay, and the noun is a church seat for clergy.

clue.text: Poisonous element in medicines, rarely on the counter

indicators.note: counter means running in the opposite direction, so the found letters are read backwards
in says the letters are found within the words that follow, spanning them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A poison seldom found in medicines you can buy over the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' suggests a pharmacy shelf, but a counter here means going against, so the letters run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a chemical element famous as a poison.

clue.text: Use loaf touring free state

indicators.note: touring means going all round a place, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece
to use material is to work it into something new, so the letters are refashioned

parts.note: the letters as printed
to rid is to free, as in rid of pests

explanation.surface: Advice to idle away time touring a US state for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' suggests lazing about; it is just four letters to be put to new use.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Number one regent, surprisingly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at things turning out unexpectedly, so the letters of the title come out in a new order

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A sovereign's stand-in turning out, unexpectedly, to be number one.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number.

clue.text: Where marathon racers compete some time later

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: in a race of great distance
second meaning: eventually, over an extended period

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is read literally first: a marathon is a race of great length.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means eventually or over time, which matches 'some time later'.
